discoveries.title: Ministry of Justice launches AI court transcription study to slash victim costs
discoveries.summary: The UK government announced research into using its in-house 'Justice Transcribe' AI tool to generate court transcripts, potentially making them free for Crown Court victims from spring 2027. Current transcripts cost hundreds or thousands of pounds, creating barriers to justice access.

discoveries.title: SRA publishes detailed AI framework with outcome-based regulation
discoveries.summary: SRA delivered webinar in February 2026 outlining framework for AI use by law firms, emphasizing outcome-based approach with explainability requirements. SRA research due April 2026 shows third of public using GenAI for legal issues, raising concerns about accuracy and confidentiality.

discoveries.title: Legal AI funding explodes with $2.3B in Q1 2026, three companies capture 63%
discoveries.summary: Legal tech funding reached $2.34 billion in Q1 2026 across 103 deals, but Relativity ($720M debt facility), Harvey ($200M at $11B valuation) and Legora ($550M at $5.55B) dominated. The concentration suggests market bifurcation between well-funded leaders and smaller players with $1M median rounds.

discoveries.title: EU AI Act enforcement begins August 2026 with high-risk system requirements
discoveries.summary: The EU AI Act's main enforcement date of August 2, 2026 triggers comprehensive obligations for high-risk AI systems, including those used in legal contexts. Legal AI systems in administration of justice are specifically covered under Annex III with requirements for documentation, risk management and human oversight.

discoveries.title: Travers Smith spins out Jylo as standalone legal AI software business
discoveries.summary: UK firm Travers Smith spun out its AI technology products including YCNBot and Analyse into new software company Jylo, with former director Shawn Curran as CEO. The move reflects law firms pivoting from internal AI development to commercializing their tools for the broader legal market.
discoveries.verification_needed: Confirm current status of Jylo and whether it has secured external customers beyond Travers Smith

discoveries.title: AI-native law firms raise $60M+ rounds as new service delivery model emerges
discoveries.summary: AI-native law firm Lawhive raised $60M Series B to expand in US, joining Crosby ($60M) in demonstrating investor appetite for AI-first legal service delivery models. These firms combine human lawyers with AI platforms rather than selling software to traditional firms, suggesting fundamental shift in professional services structure.
